quotes.text: This is a national security issue. We will not compete with China. We are at an arms race in artificial intelligence with China, and we don't have the mineral production, the mining, the processing, the refining to be competitive.

Would you agree that we are in a technology arms race with China for dominance in AI and quantum computing? [...] the bottom line is is that it is going to require enormous amounts of power [...] they are really focused on hydrocarbon coal-based power generation. [...] and this is the existential threat to the United States. It is also a threat to our economy. [...] I think ensuring that we maximize our access to high energy density [...] is not just an economic issue. It is a national security issue [...]

My concern too is we are in an arms race for artificial intelligence. And I am looking at the NERC report on the high-risk areas and the medium-risk areas, and it is clear we don't have the power capacity to build the data systems that we need in order to win that arms race with China.
We are in an arms race with China for artificial intelligence and quantum computing. What amount of power generation, in addition to what we have now, will we need?

If we lose the arms race in artificial intelligence and quantum computing to China, they will be the superpower, not a superpower. [...] One of the things that I think we need to be taking a look at in addition to the power generation is our dependence on China for critical minerals and rare earth elements.
What do you consider a greater threat to our future national security, losing the AI arms race to China or climate change?
My concern is that we are in an arms race with China for artificial intelligence and quantum computing, and that if China wins that race they will not be a superpower, they will be the superpower.

considering that we are in an arms race for artificial intelligence with China, should not we be looking at rather than investing in more renewables, investing in nuclear or maybe more hydrocarbon, power generation so that we will have the ability to power the data centers that we are going to need to compete in AI.

We are also seeing a lot of unwanted and scam robotexts, and AI generated phone calls and text messages, including voice clones and deepfakes. [...] In August, the FCC proposed rules to protect consumers from AI-generated robocalls and robotexts.
In August, the FCC proposed rules to protect consumers from AI-generated robocalls and robotexts. These are steps in the right direction, and I applaud the coordination we have seen thus far.
We are in an arms race for artificial intelligence and quantum computing with China. And in order to meet that, we are going to have to have some permitting reform.

this race for artificial intelligence is for one thing only, and that is to determine who will be the superpower. Whoever wins this race will not be a superpower; they will be the superpower. [...] So one of my main objectives right now is to get this critical infrastructure built [...] so that we can decouple ourselves from China in that regard. It is absolutely a top national security issue.
